thread:
ollie: @sam @mara heads up — SapphireCap hit us with a perf regression after we flipped the new kernel selector. They run on Dedicated, steady QPS ~220 r/s, and tail latency jumped ~40% this morning. Can we look at batching/queue/token-budget?

sam: Can you paste the p99 and token distribution? is this across all models or one family?

mara: Also need KV cache hit rate and any recent kernel hints (fused vs baseline).

ollie: Quick snapshot from their profiler (30s window):
```
model: gpt-large-v1
QPS: 220
p50: 35ms p95: 110ms p99: 420ms
avg tokens/request: 420
batch formation: median batch size 3 (expected 6)
KV cache hit rate: 68% (down from 92% pre-change)
kernel hints: forced -> fused_attn_v2 on nodes pool-ded-8
```
ollie: They say queue backs up and small batches keep getting scheduled. token-budget currently 800, max_queue_ms 80.

zheng: Looks like two interacting issues: fused_attn_v2 has slightly worse cold-start throughput for short sequences and our continuous batching heuristic is shrinking batches when KV misses increase. KV thrash (68%) means more wasted tokens and earlier flushes.

sam: For a dedicated customer we can propose a targeted config: increase token_budget -> 1200, bump max_queue_ms -> 120, enable kv_prefetch: true, and set batch_min_size: 4 to avoid too-small microbatches. Also add kernel_selector hint fallback to baseline when batch_size < 4. Example config: 
```json
{
  "token_budget": 1200,
  "max_queue_ms": 120,
  "kv_prefetch": true,
  "batch_min_size": 4,
  "kernel_selector": ["fused_attn_v2","baseline_fused_attn"]
}
```

ollie: That aligns with my read. Any risk to overall throughput/cost for other tenants on the same dedicated pool? This is SapphireCap reserved, so should be fine but want to flag cost delta.

mara: Suggest a gradual canary: apply to 10% of their capacity for 2 hours, measure p95/p99, KV hit, and avg batch size. If p99 drops 20% and batch size increases to ~5-6, we promote. Add an autoscale guard to revert if tail > 600ms.

runtime-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled: sapphirecap/dedicated/policy-1964209876 -> 10% at 1964210500 (ETA 5m). Logs will be posted to #eng-runtime-deploys. :rocket:

sam: I'll own the canary checks and the rollback hook. @ollie can you get SapphireCap ops on a short call so they can validate client-side behavior?

ollie: Yep — pinged their SRE, scheduled 10:30. Will update thread after the canary window. :eyes:

mara: Thanks — if the canary shows improvement we'll draft a formal change note and updated capacity estimate for their billing.

ollie: Updating thread after first 30m: initial 30m canary (10%) shows p99 -> 250ms (from 420ms), KV hit -> 87%, median batch size -> 5. No regressions on other metrics. Continuing to 2h window.

sam: Great, looks promising. Next steps: apply to 50% for 1h, monitor, then full flip if stable.
